channel.title: Kompas — News
channel.description: Key news on repression in Russia and against those who left: political prisoners, verdicts, new designations. Every item links to its source. Updated morning and evening.

item.title: FSB officers detain Izhevsk activist Dmitry Morozov, who sought a rally against election fraud
item.description: According to his father, Morozov had a battered face and swollen hands during a search; officers spoke of links to banned organisations. Relatives and lawyers do not know where he is. — Mediazona

item.title: Germany refuses a Russian student a study visa, citing a 'security threat'
item.description: According to the Molniya project, the embassy in Moscow turned down a graduate of the HSE design programme. The rights group calls it a dangerous precedent for art students. — Meduza

item.title: Ukrainian Lyubov Rozhanskaya detained in Astana at Russia's request; Russia seeks her extradition
item.description: According to DW, cited by Mediazona, Russia accuses her of attempting to abduct her grandson. Her lawyers say she did not know about the case and has never been to Russia. — Mediazona

item.title: Prosecutors seek 5 years 11 months in absentia for Masyanya creator Oleg Kuvaev
item.description: According to Mediazona, he is charged under Articles 330.1 and 280.4 over an episode in which Masyanya urges Russian soldiers to surrender. His lawyer says Kuvaev was not notified of the case. — Mediazona

item.title: Journalist Roman Ivanov, jailed over army 'fakes', sent to a punishment cell for 14 days
item.description: According to his lawyer, the reason is unknown and he may be moved to a strict regime. Ivanov is serving 7 years in penal colony No. 6 in Kolomna over posts about Bucha and other war crimes. — Mediazona

item.title: Photojournalist Artem Chernov put on the wanted list
item.description: According to Mediazona, he was added to the Interior Ministry's wanted database; details of the criminal case are unknown. Chernov told the outlet he had not known about the prosecution. — Mediazona

item.title: Georgian court releases on bail Sergei Furgal's former aide, whom Russia wants extradited
item.description: According to The Insider, Mikhail Timofeev was released on bail of 50 thousand lari and barred from leaving Georgia. In September a court approved his extradition, but the UN Human Rights Committee told Georgia not to extradite him. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: Justice Ministry adds Zhanna Nemtsova and Navalny Team to 'foreign agents' register
item.description: According to OVD-Info, Circassian activist Rustam Khuazhev and the resource Reanimatsiya were also added. In September Nemtsova was placed on an international wanted list. — OVD-Info

item.title: Defendant in Artpodgotovka case tells court FSB officers tortured him for three days
item.description: Sergei Yakovlev says that after the torture he was forced to assemble a bomb for an operational video, OVD-Info reports, citing Mediazona's courtroom coverage. — OVD-Info

item.title: Tomsk court remands producer Elena Matushevskaya in custody over donations to FBK
item.description: According to OVD-Info, investigators say she transferred money to FBK seven times, 3500 roubles in total (Article 282.3). Matushevskaya lived in Serbia; her defence will appeal. — OVD-Info

item.title: Founder of Buryat independence movement sentenced in absentia to 20 years
item.description: A military court in Chita sentenced US-based Marina Khankhalaeva under Articles 282.2 and 205.5, Buryatia's police said, 7x7 reports. According to the outlet, the verdict was handed down on 27 August. — 7x7

item.title: Belarus designates YouTube channel with Sergei Tikhanovsky's poems 'extremist'
item.description: The Oshmyany district court made the decision on 25 September, according to the updated Information Ministry list, Mediazona Belarus reports. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: Belarus: 22-year-old college graduate from Babruysk convicted of 'facilitating extremism'
item.description: Mogilev regional court sentenced Yuliana Molochkova to restricted freedom at home under Article 361-4, Part 1, Mediazona Belarus reports, citing Nasha Niva. The exact term is unknown. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: Astra founder Anastasia Chumakova sentenced in absentia to seven years in a penal colony
item.description: Mediazona reports that the Zavolzhsky District Court in Ulyanovsk convicted her of spreading military 'fakes' and breaching the 'foreign agent' law. The journalist has lived outside Russia for several years. — Mediazona

item.title: Seriously ill Crimean woman in Simferopol pre-trial detention has gone two months without medicine and insulin
item.description: 58-year-old Tatiana Begey wrote this in a letter, OVD-Info reports, citing FREE120. She has diabetes and serious kidney failure and is accused of illegal possession of weapons and passing on secret information. — OVD-Info

item.title: Court refuses to find punishment-cell placement of Perm political prisoner on day of family visit unlawful
item.description: The Verkhneuralsk District Court rejected Anton Galeta's claim and his demand for 20 thousand roubles in compensation, 7x7 reports. According to his support group, his relatives had come to visit him for the first time in four years, but the visit was banned. — 7x7

item.title: Former TV2 employee who lived in Serbia detained in Krasnoyarsk over donations to FBK
item.description: Elena Matushevskaya is suspected of taking part in an 'extremist' organisation, Novaya Gazeta Europe reports, citing Govorit NeMoskva. She had come to Krasnoyarsk for work; a custody hearing is expected in Tomsk. — Novaya Gazeta Europe

item.title: Case against Lida Moniava, founder of the Dom s Mayakom hospice, taken over by Investigative Committee headquarters
item.description: According to her lawyer Mikhail Biryukov, the case was due to go to court on 30 September. Moniava is accused of spreading 'fakes' about the army over a Telegram post, Meduza reports. — Meduza

item.title: Former medical centre director in Inza, convicted in 'LGBT movement' case, faces 'satanism movement' charge
item.description: Zhuravlev is accused of taking part in the 'international satanism movement', designated 'extremist', Mediazona reports, citing the Prison Lawyer project. Last spring he was sentenced to three years in a colony. — Mediazona

item.title: Belarus: 26-year-old IT specialist sentenced to five years for donations
item.description: Minsk City Court convicted Mikhail Filipenko of taking part in military action abroad (Part 2 of Article 361-3) and fined him 500 base units, Mediazona Belarus reports, citing the Viasna centre. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: Leaked Turkmen interior ministry wanted list shows persecution of critics abroad
item.description: According to Turkmen.news and OCCRP, 613 people were on the wanted list at the end of 2022, 93 of them facing political charges, including 'terrorism'. — Turkmen.news

item.title: Belarusian political prisoner Vadim Zdorovennov sentenced to 4 years and 7 months in a new case
item.description: According to Viasna, cited by Mediazona Belarus, he was convicted under Articles 342, 130 and 203-1 of the Criminal Code. He had earlier received two years for insulting Lukashenko and was due for release in November 2026. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: First person charged under Russia's 'confidential cooperation' with foreigners article released
item.description: Pavel Pishchulin from Penza region served his full term and was released on 17 September from a penal colony in Kirovo-Chepetsk, he told Mediazona. He was detained in October 2022 after talking to undercover FSB officers. — Mediazona

item.title: Kamchatka: 68-year-old disabled pensioner sentenced to 14 years for treason
item.description: The Kamchatka regional court sentenced Valery Dobrovolsky to 14 years in a strict-regime colony (Article 275), Mediazona reports, citing the court's press office. Memorial has recognised him as a political prisoner. — Mediazona

item.title: Yaroslavl court sentences exiled LGBT activist to 4 years in absentia
item.description: The Kirovsky district court found Yaroslav Sirotkin guilty of taking part in an 'extremist' organisation (Part 2 of Article 282.2) and of breaching the 'foreign agent' law, 7x7 reports, citing Pervy Otdel. — 7x7

item.title: Tula artist held in pre-trial detention since February over 17 memes about depression and suicide
item.description: According to Mediazona, Anna Luginina is charged under Article 110.2 over memes in an abandoned VKontakte group she started before she came of age. — Mediazona

item.title: Russia agrees with five CIS countries to share data on people the authorities deem 'extremists'
item.description: The prosecutors general of Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan signed an agreement to share information on organisations and individuals, Meduza reports, citing RBC. — Meduza

item.title: Moscow court arrests journalist Yury Dud in absentia on a charge of justifying terrorism
item.description: The Basmanny court arrested Dud in absentia under Part 2 of Article 205.2, the Moscow courts' press service said. The Investigative Committee claims the case stems from his interview with RDK founder Denis Kapustin. — Mediazona

item.title: St Petersburg man jailed for 6 years over three UNIAN reposts
item.description: According to Mediazona, the Nevsky district court gave Yegor Gulyaev six years in a war 'fakes' case (Part 2(d) of Article 207.3) over VKontakte reposts; prosecutors had sought 12 years. — Mediazona

item.title: Blogger in Adygea remanded over a form sent to the Anti-War Committee
item.description: The Maikop city court remanded a blogger in custody until 23 November; he is charged with taking part in a terrorist organisation (Part 2 of Article 205.5) for sending a form on Telegram, the court's website says. — Mediazona

item.title: Activist Mavlyan Askarbekov sentenced to two years in Bishkek
item.description: According to Azattyq, the Leninsky district court found Askarbekov guilty of inciting hatred over Facebook posts; the case was run by the GKNB. The activist rejected the charges. — Azattyq Asia

item.title: Former Lida police officer's eight-year treason sentence comes to light
item.description: The Grodno regional court sentenced Sergei Kazinsky to eight years (Article 356) back in 2023, the Viasna human rights centre reports; he left the police after the events of 2020. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: Prosecutor seeks four years for activist Mavlyan Askarbekov in Bishkek
item.description: According to lawyer Erik Iriskulbekov, quoted by Azattyq, the case of inciting hatred was investigated by the GKNB; on 29 September Askarbekov is to give his final statement, after which a verdict is expected. — Azattyq Asia

item.title: More than 150 human rights defenders urge Kazakhstan not to extradite Emelyanova and Movlaev to Russia
item.description: According to Vlast, the appeal was signed by 155 people, among them members of OVD-Info and First Department. They ask for a diplomatic corridor to a safe third country. — Vlast.kz

item.title: Journalist Shamshad Agha rejects the charges at the Meydan TV trial in Baku
item.description: According to JAMnews, on 28 September at the Baku Serious Crimes Court the founder of Arqument.az called the case fabricated and linked his arrest to his journalism. — JAMnews

item.title: Prosecutors seek 12 years for a St Petersburg man accused of army ‘fakes’ over three UNIAN reposts
item.description: According to Mediazona, prosecutors at St Petersburg's Nevsky District Court asked for 12 years in a general-regime colony for Gulyaev (Article 207.3, part 2, point ‘d’). He has been in custody throughout the investigation and trial. — Mediazona

item.title: Protest in New York against Kazakhstan extraditing activists Emelyanova and Movlaev to Russia
item.description: According to Azattyq Asia, Iuliia Emelianova and Mansur Movlaev have been held in a remand prison in Almaty for over a year after being detained at Moscow's request. Kazakhstan earlier refused Movlaev asylum. — Azattyq Asia

item.title: Minsk woman, 58, convicted over protest participation and insulting Lukashenko
item.description: According to Nasha Niva, cited by Mediazona Belarus, Minsk's Pershamaiski District Court convicted Oksana Marinina under Articles 368 and 342 of the Criminal Code and sentenced her to restricted freedom at home; the exact term is unknown. — Mediazona Belarus

item.title: Political analyst Alexander Kynev beaten during arrest, now in the hospital at Matrosskaya Tishina remand prison
item.description: According to the Slovo Zashchite project, Kynev was diagnosed with two tibia fractures, allegedly the result of torture. His lawyer could neither confirm nor deny the reports of violence. — Mediazona

item.title: FSB opens a case for membership of a terrorist organisation against London-based Ksenia Maksimova
item.description: Maksimova heads the Russian Democratic Society in the UK. The FSB claims she raised money through the movement "in the interests of the Kyiv regime". She was put on the wanted list on 16 September. — Mediazona
